title: Research with a gate

proposed_identity.status: historical precedent only; L13-L16 purpose-specific rights pending

presenter_passages.passage_exact: Morgan opens Harbor's paper planning folder on Friday. The Session Option Brief is still held because no one has confirmed staffing. An idea appears in the margin: perhaps a different brief format would make the next review easier.
Harbor has a proposal that someone can inspect, and a clear record that nothing has run.

offscreen_narration.text:
It is tempting to let the preparation agent change the format and declare an improvement. But Harbor has no baseline for review time, no test plan, and no permission to change the team's process. The honest first artifact is a proposal.

Chapter Twenty-Three separates five states: propose, not run, gate, trace, then approve or discard. For the Harbor case, the proposed question is narrow: would a brief that puts staffing evidence first help Morgan identify a hold faster? The hypothesis needs a comparison and a metric. We could compare two course brief layouts in a paper exercise. We cannot claim one works better because it looks cleaner to us. The `not_run` state records exactly what is missing.

The workbook's AutoResearch Proposal asks for the baseline, experiment configuration, expected impact, touched settings, metric gate, risk, rollback, approval question, and next gate. Here the baseline is `unknown`, not zero. The proposed metric is whether a reviewer correctly identifies the staffing hold, with time to find it as a secondary observation. No result exists yet. The touched surface would be the paper brief layout only. The rollback is to keep the current layout. No routing default, memory record, or real calendar changes.

Morgan owns the review of the proposal because Morgan owns this planning decision. A real experiment would need a fresh, scoped approval and an appropriate participant and privacy plan. This lesson grants none of that. In the paper scenario, Morgan can reject the idea, ask for a clearer baseline, or authorize a later bounded test. The agent cannot turn a promising hypothesis into durable memory. A memory proposal would need its own source, scope, expiry, and human decision.

Write a `not_run` reason that another person can act on: `No agreed comparison set or reviewer protocol; staffing hold remains unresolved.` Then add the next safe step: Morgan reviews whether the question is worth testing at all. If Morgan says no, keep the rejection and its reason. If Morgan says yes, define the test before anyone runs it. Either path teaches Harbor something about its priorities. A silent queue of ideas teaches almost nothing.

Pause on your own workflow type. What evidence would make your favorite improvement worth testing?

Draft one AutoResearch Proposal. Name the question, hypothesis, comparison, current baseline, primary metric and guardrail, expected direction, risk, touched surface, rollback, owner, approval question, and next metric gate. Mark the result `not_run`. Write the reason in plain language and the action Morgan may take after review. Keep the staffing and spend holds visible. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data, run a provider, contact anyone, change a setting, or promote a finding.

Save revision thirteen as a draft. Research begins when a question can survive a gate, not when a dashboard fills with experiments.

continuity.source_ids_policy: protected synthetic trace only; no source IDs in provider request

gates: purpose-specific L13-L16 look and voice approval
fresh provider quote, balance and enforceable one-job and batch caps
native audio timing and sentence-level edit audit
caption, diagram alt, mobile/desktop and final MP4 review
stop_conditions: source, rights, identity, voice or packet drift
uncertain job outcome or provider error; no retry
cost cap uncertainty or unexpected debit
narration omission, repetition or altered meaning
visual clipping, label collision or unreadable captions
